matchupAnalysis: The model makes Nurmagomedov a 79.7% favourite, with the GBM at 81.1% and the hand-tuned path at 82.9% — unusually tight agreement for a five-round main event. The case rests almost entirely on two composites: grappling +2.23 and output +1.97, the two largest single-fighter readings anywhere on this card. Song is not weak on either axis so much as ordinary — grappling −0.10, output +0.59 — and the gap between those columns is what the simulation keeps converting into control time. Nurmagomedov's underlying rates support it: a +2.00 strike differential, 79.4% takedown defence and a +0.359 control differential against Song's +0.50 and +0.044.

What the numbers do not describe is a finisher. Nurmagomedov's power sits at −0.04, dead average for bantamweight, and his UFC finish rate is 37.5% with only 12.5% by knockout. Song is the more dangerous man in any single exchange — power +0.40, a 41.7% KO rate across seventeen UFC fights, and the sim still credits him 8.8% by knockout despite losing overall. The decision edge of +2.479 is the second-largest on the card and the fight's real shape: Nurmagomedov wins 45.1% of the time on the scorecards, more than double his 22.4% by KO and 12.2% by submission combined.

The five-round distance is where this becomes interesting for totals. The fight goes to a decision 52.3% of the time and clears Over 4.5 rounds at 56.1%, which is not a grinder's number — Nurmagomedov has never been finished in nine UFC fights, while Song has been finished in 20% of his. Nurmagomedov also carries a 212-day layoff against Song's 86, the largest gap in the top half of the card, and his own last defeat was a five-round decision to Dvalishvili. Song arrives on a submission win over Figueiredo; his only recent loss was a decision to O'Malley.

synopsis.body: Nurmagomedov 79.7% — the clearest read on the card, and a positional one rather than a violent one. His grappling (+2.23) and output (+1.97) are the two biggest composite readings of the night, but his power is exactly average and the model routes 45.1% of his wins through the judges. Song remains live as the only real knockout threat in the fight. Over 4.5 rounds at 56.1% reflects a favourite who controls rather than finishes, against an opponent who has never been stopped by anyone of this style.

The counter-argument is narrow but real: Borjas's only positive composite is wrestling defence (+0.65), aimed squarely at Tsuruya's one weapon, and he beat Andre Lima two months ago.
